title: Banxico holds rates unchanged at 6.50% unanimously
summary: On Thursday, the Bank of Mexico, also known as Banxico, decided to hold interest rates unchanged at 6.50% for the fourth time, as expected, in a unanimous vote.

title: Italy Returns to Nuclear After 40-Year Hiatus
summary: For the first time in nearly four decades, Italy is considering nuclear power as part of its energy calculus. The Italian Senate on Wednesday gave final approval to a government plan to restart nuclear power generation, Reuters said, almost 40 years after a referendum led to the closure of Italy’s reactors: The government aims to deploy advanced modular reactors to help decarbonise industry and strengthen energy security, arguing that technological and safety advances have rendered the 1987 anti-nuclear vote obsolete. title: Mexican Peso slides to April lows as Banxico shrugs off Fed gap
summary: The Mexican Peso extended its losses against the US Dollar on Thursday after the Bank of Mexico (Banxico) held the benchmark interest rate unchanged at 6.50%, disregarding the interest rate differential as a primary factor in setting monetary policy.

title: Global Biofuels Output Could Surge 70% Amid Energy Crisis
summary: Global biofuels production is projected to surge by nearly 70% by 2030 as major producing countries raise their fuel-blending mandates in response to the energy crisis triggered by the Middle East conflict, a study co-authored by British think tank Chatham House and Forest Stewardship Council has found. Biofuels like ethanol, which typically originate from food crops or animal feed and are mixed with gasoline or diesel, become more cost-competitive as crude oil and gasoline prices spike. Norwegian Krone: Norges Bank hike supports currency – BBH
summary: Brown Brothers Harriman’s (BBH) Elias Haddad highlights that the Norwegian Krone (NOK) outperformed after Norges Bank delivered a hawkish 25 basis point hike to 4.50%.

title: Germany faces energy tax losses as EV sales rise
summary: The rapid shift to electric vehicles in Germany is cutting fuel tax revenue for the government. As EV sales surge, policymakers face growing pressure to find new ways to fund roads and transportation infrastructure.

title: Iran sees air, land travel chaos as US sanctions bite
summary: Flights between Iran and the United Arab Emirates have been suspended, following tighter US sanctions on Iran's aviation industry. The move effectively cuts Tehran off from Dubai, one of the region's most important commercial hubs. There are also huge backups near Iran's border with Turkey, as overland shipping routes struggle to fill the gaps.
